_readme: One entry per training job that can run on the Google Cloud GPU. `source` is the sibling repo folder (relative to the folder holding the Po repos) that is packed and shipped; `cwd` is where the trainer runs inside it; `setup` prepares the Linux environment; `command` is the trainer command the repo already uses locally, with {hours} replaced by the time budget. Commands run on Linux (bash, forward slashes, no .venv/Scripts), so they are not the Windows commands. `excludes` are paths relative to `source` that never leave this PC (Unity Library/Temp/Build, .venv, .git, old runs); `artifacts` are directories the job writes that are streamed to Cloud Storage while it runs and pulled back with `pull`. Runbook: docs/gcp-training.md.

jobs.label: Streetball curriculum queue (l1 -> l4, gates, ONNX export)
jobs.notes: Needs the sibling shared/obs_spec.json (version_tags hashes it) and writes docs/<date>/ reports; both travel with the source tree. torch is pinned to 2.14.1+cu130 from the explicit cu130 index, so the VM driver must be >= 580.

jobs.label: PoBox queue runner (works through training/logs/queue.json)
jobs.notes: The on-disk folder is training (lower case) - Windows hides that, Linux does not. The queue resumes from training/checkpoints/shipped (67 MB, ships with the tarball) and training/logs/queue.json. PyPI torch on Linux is already the CUDA build, so no extra uv pip step is needed.

jobs.label: Slap Unreal v5 retrain queue (Mom/Tong L1-L4 + G1 get-up)
jobs.setup: uv venv --python 3.10 .venv && uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -r requirements.txt && uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python --torch-backend=auto torch
jobs.notes: overnight.py resolves --queue against training/runs, so runs/retrain_v5_queue.json travels with the tree. --torch-backend=auto picks the CUDA wheel that matches the VM driver.
